PROOF.ARM_BOUND_AND_EXHAUSTIVE_M_RANGE: W=sum C(deg_G(v),2)=816, and each triangle occupies three centered wedges, so O=816-3T. For an edge hl let k be its common-neighbor count. Its open-wedge arm count is 11+deg_G(l)-2-2k. Since k<=deg_G(l)-1, this is at least 4 for degree 7 and at least 5 for degree 6. Each open wedge has two arms, so 4c<=2O, hence O>=4m. For T>=256, O<=48 and m<=12 (c<=24). For m>=13, T<=floor((816-52)/3)=254. Therefore the m=0..12 table together with this tail covers every graph, not just a sampled range.
PROOF.BOTH_CROSS_TRIANGLE_TYPES: For each l in L, its b_l neighbors in H supply C(b_l,2) pairs. Subtract the pairs in F: Z_FB=sum_{hh' in F}|N_B(h) intersect N_B(h')|. Thus C_HHL=sum_l C(b_l,2)-Z_FB. Likewise C_HLL=sum_h C(a_h,2)-Z_MB, where Z_MB=sum_{ll' in M}|N_B(l) intersect N_B(l')|. These count the two disjoint cross-triangle types exactly, including every incidence and internal adjacency.
PROOF.CLIQUE_MINUS_MISSING_EDGES: For any missing-edge graph Q on n vertices, each missing edge lies in n-2 triples. Two missing edges share a triple exactly when they share a vertex; there are A_Q=sum_v C(deg_Q(v),2) such pairs. Three missing edges share a triple exactly for a triangle of Q. No triple has more than three edges. Inclusion-exclusion therefore gives triangles(K_n-Q)=C(n,3)-(n-2)|Q|+A_Q-t_Q. Applying this to F and M gives T_H=220-10m+A_F-t_F and T_L=50-6m+A_M-t_M.

PROOF.DEFINITIONS_AND_SIMULTANEOUS_CONSTRAINTS: G is a simple undirected graph with H of size 12 and L of size 8. F=K12-G[H], M=K8-G[L], and B=G[H,L]. Put a_h=deg_F(h), q_l=deg_M(l), delta_l=7-deg_G(l), b_l=deg_B(l). Delta is 1 at exactly the two degree-6 vertices and 0 elsewhere. Degree equations give deg_B(h)=a_h<=8 and b_l=q_l-delta_l>=0, with q_l<=7, b_l<=12 and q_l>=1 at both delta vertices. Summing the H equations gives c=2|F|=2m. Summing L gives 54=2|G[L]|+c, so |G[L]|=27-m and |M|=m+1. Thus sum a=sum b=2m and sum q=2m+2. All equations hold simultaneously in the same graph; B must be a binary incidence matrix with these row and column sums. Independent maxima below are only upper relaxations, never certificates of joint feasibility.
PROOF.DEGREE_SEQUENCE_CERTIFICATE_COMPLETENESS: Sort the positive degrees of F or M; pad with zero degrees to 12 or 8 vertices. For a graph with e edges this is a nonincreasing integer partition of 2e, with at most n parts and each part at most the degree cap. The partitions recursion enumerates every such partition exactly: choose the first positive part p, then recurse on total-p with next cap p and one fewer available part; induction on the remaining total proves completeness. For any k vertices of largest degrees, their degree sum is at most k(k-1)+sum_{i>k}min(d_i,k), by counting internal and external edges. Hence every graph passes all inequalities in erdos_gallai. Filtering by these necessary inequalities cannot remove a valid graph; sufficiency of the inequalities is not needed for the proof. The Havel-Hakimi comparison is only a consistency check. The scan maximizes S_F with 2m total and cap 8, and S_M-q_y1-q_y2 with 2m+2 total and cap 7. Both delta vertices have positive q, so subtracting the two smallest positive parts safely upper-bounds the latter quantity for every placement. Thus T<=270-20m+U_F(m)+V_M(m+1), with no claim that separate maximizers share a feasible B. This is exhaustive bounded degree accounting justified by necessary conditions; it is not a full graph census, random test, or replacement for the identity proof.

Adding all four triangle types yields T=270-16m+A_F+A_M-t_F-t_M+C_HHL+C_HLL =272-16m+2A_F+2A_M-Y-Z. Since 2A_F=S_F-2m and 2A_M=S_M-2m-2, this is exactly T=270-20m+S_F+S_M-Y-Z. Every term of Z is nonnegative. This is an algebraic proof for every graph in the domain, independent of example checks. The packet's tentative formula with negative A_F,A_M and negative actual cross-triangle counts has incorrect signs and is replaced by the proved identities above.

PROOF.M12_EQUALITY_CONTRADICTION: The necessary-degree scan gives U_F(12)=108 and V_M(13)=118, so the relaxed upper bound is 256. T=256 would force both maxima and Z=0. The sole M degree sequence maximizing V_M is (7,7,2,2,2,2,2,2). In any simple graph with this sequence, the two degree-7 vertices are adjacent to all other seven vertices. Their edge with each of the six others forms a distinct triangle, so t_M>=6, contradicting Z=0. This uses mandatory adjacency, not failure to construct a graph. Independently, the sole F maximizer (8,5,2,2,2,2,1,1,1) requires an H vertex with all eight L neighbors, including both degree-6 vertices. At T=256 and m=12, 4c=2O=96 would require every cross arm to equal 4; each such degree-6 incidence has at least 5 arms, also a contradiction. Thus the maxima cannot simultaneously produce a valid equality case, and T<=255 for m=12.
